title: fix: tighten short auth screens and dialog footers
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Short auth screens (dashboard sign-in, Enter sign-in, device, errors) used the busy consent layout: a 576px card, 36px buttons, and on phones the only action sat at the bottom of an otherwise empty screen.

- Dialog actions follow the content and only stick to the bottom once it scrolls. Footer buttons are 48px; they share the row in narrow dialogs (below 36rem, phones included) and a lone action spans it
- Auth screens default to the 448px card (consent and top-up keep `lg`); loading is centred; footnote links are quiet and wrap into balanced lines
- Sign-in titles name what you sign in to: "Sign in to {app}" on dashboards, "Sign in to Pollinations, to continue to {app host}" on the OAuth step for any OAuth app. No admin claim or colour-mode switch there; the consent text between the cards is trimmed
- Buttons follow the button rule: a screen's single main action that doesn't write uses the filled button, busy buttons keep full strength with a spinner, and "Back to app" is large with a back arrow
- Device code: Continue only for a complete code, busy while checking, frozen after a rejected code until it changes; the code length is shared with the server and dashes are ignored

gist.headline: Sign-in finds its footing
gist.blurb: Short sign-in screens no longer dress up as lengthy consent forms. The button stays close to the question, and device codes wait until they’re complete.
gist.summary: Auth screens now use 448px cards instead of 576px consent-sized cards, keep 48px dialog actions near their content until scrolling requires a sticky footer, and validate device codes using a length shared with the server.
gist.impact: On phones, sign-in actions are easier to reach; device-code Continue activates only for a complete code, ignores dashes, and waits for a changed code after a rejection.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy pixel-art sign-in screen on a small phone, with one clear button directly below the form rather than stranded at the bottom. Polli, wearing tiny reading glasses, checks a completed device-code card; a small vine and flowers soften the scene.
